text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Friday:
- Swiss women take better care of their health than Swiss men but consider themselves less healthy, says Switzerland's first official report on women's health.

- Swiss publisher Ringier will close weekely lifestyle magazine Schweizer Woche after next week's issue due to dwindling sales. Thirty-five employees will lose their jobs. - Switzerland wants to ban imports of German meat starting January 1 due to the danger of mad cow disease.
- Jewish refugees in Switzerland received only little support from the Swiss from 1933 to 1952 and were taken care of mainly by Jewish organisations, according to a newspaper report.
- Neue Haveg AG in Baden, a seller of electronic equipment, is liquidating due to financial difficulty. Some 85 employees will lose their jobs.
- Nearly 8,000 students protested in Zurich on Thursday evening against planned budget cuts in education, including the decrease in elective courses offered and the increase in class size.
- The Swiss government is proposing to completely slash unemployment insurance and benefits for job seekers under the age of 20.
- Klaus Schwab, Founder and President of the World Economic Forum, has been named Vice President of the SMH board of directors.

- Union Bank of Switzerland is closing three of its branches in Geneva as part of an overall trimming of its Swiss domestic business, including closing 30 of 295 national branches. Some 47 jobs will be cut.
